chunks: Al-Saffar narrated from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Abi Sa'id al-Khurasani, who said:

Two men entered upon Abi al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام in Khurasan and asked him about shortening the prayer. He said to one of them: Shortening has become obligatory upon you, because you intended me. And he said to the other: Completing the prayer in full has become obligatory upon you, because you intended the ruler.

key_terms.التَّمَامُ: performing the prayer in full without shortening
key_terms.خُرَاسَانَ: Khurasan, the region where this event occurred
key_terms.قَصَدْتَنِي: you intended me as your destination

ai.seo_question: When must a traveler shorten the prayer and when must it be prayed in full according to Imam al-Rida عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about prayer in travel based on the traveler's intended destination and purpose. Imam al-Rida عليه السلام distinguished between one who traveled intending him and one who traveled intending the ruler, resulting in different rulings regarding qasr and tamam.
